prompt: PizzaOrder's constructor is private, so the nested Builder is the only way to make one. Finish the builder and the order. Complete the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: A private constructor removes every other way to create the object, which is what lets the builder guarantee that a PizzaOrder is complete and valid the moment it exists. A nested class can still call that private constructor because private means "inside this top-level class", not "inside this one class body". Each builder method returning this is what allows the calls to chain, and the order copies the builder's list so a reused builder can never mutate an order that was already built.
hints: Every builder method that is not build() should end with return this; so calls can be chained.
The private constructor should read the builder's values and copy the topping list with new ArrayList<>(...), never store the builder's own list.
In topping, check the reject cases first -- null or empty name, four toppings already, or a case-insensitive match with something already added.
